customization.summary: Tested integration: agent-sandbox run with the default Google-managed Python code sandbox under an Agent Engine/Agent Runtime parent. No CPU, RAM, image, GPU or network settings are sent by the adapter. Current official BYOC templates offer image, CPU/memory requests and limits, ports and internet_access, but that separate managed-container path was not tested. GKE Agent Sandbox and Compute Engine GPU VMs are infrastructure alternatives, not capabilities measured for this adapter.

features.notes: Official BYOC uses an Artifact Registry image and a custom-container sandbox template. The tested default code sandbox has no image selector; local shell/CMEK references explicitly lack end-to-end verification.

The report verifies installing one uploaded pure-Python fixture wheel via pip --no-index --no-deps --target, then importing it. This is not online package installation or arbitrary native dependencies. Official code-sandbox docs say own libraries cannot be installed; retain this narrow observed exception rather than generalizing it. BYOC is the documented dependency-customization path.

BYOC templates document CPU requests/limits. The tested adapter requests none; its cost estimate assumes 2 vCPU, not an allocation attestation. A separate 2026-10-01 local probe saw 8 visible CPUs and roughly 2x CPU parallel speedup, neither a contractual allocation nor current-run inventory.

BYOC templates document memory requests/limits. The tested adapter requests none; 4 GB in report cost metadata is an estimate. The separate 2026-10-01 reference measured 2 GiB, illustrating why actual current allocation remains unknown.

No GPU requested/tested. Current guest inventory reports nvidia-smi unavailable, which does not establish platform-wide GPU eligibility. Reviewed BYOC example does not establish accelerator support. Compute Engine and compatible GKE GPU deployments are separate choices.

The official code sandbox has no network access; the local probe concurs, contradicting has_internet_access=true in the adapter. BYOC documents egress_control_config.internet_access. The tested adapter sends no network policy and the evaluation campaign does not attest effective policy.

Files/state survive calls within a live sandbox, not deletion. Current lifecycle docs describe filesystem-preserving pause/resume, but code-sandbox snapshots are explicitly unsupported and the adapter uses one-shot deletion. Durable cross-deletion storage and pause/resume were not tested.

Code execution can reuse state by sandbox ID. Local start/exec supports this, but this adapter calls run for every execution and does not retain a remote session. Current docs advertise up to 14 days; the bundled CLI caps TTL at 3600s and the adapter caps its requested TTL at 900s.

The offline-wheel workload executes a pip subprocess inside the code sandbox. Local tooling also documents bash via the code sandbox. This does not attest a separately provisioned shell-container sandbox under CMEK.

The evaluation verifies a 26900-byte artifact round trip by expected size and SHA-256 and verifies summary.json. The adapter passes --upload and reads output files. Official request/response limit is 100 MB in aggregate; unlimited stdout rendering is not unlimited API payload size.
BYOC templates document ports. That is not evidence of an automatically public preview URL. The tested code adapter has no port exposure or preview integration.
This service is Google-managed. A locally running client does not self-host its sandbox. Kubernetes-SIGs/GKE Agent Sandbox and Compute Engine VMs are separate infrastructure deployments.

CMEK is configured at parent runtime creation and inherited by sandboxes/templates/snapshots for at-rest content, not resource metadata. Local setup observed a need for both Vertex service agents. The saved evaluation lacks parent/key readback and KMS audit evidence, so encryption is not measured by that report.

pricing.model: Allocated Agent Compute vCPU-hours plus Agent Memory GiB-hours; official usage rounded to the nearest second. Separate KMS and other resource costs may apply.
pricing.limitations: Reviewed 2026-10-13. Official pricing includes monthly free usage per account of 50 compute hours and 100 GiB-hours of RAM and eligible savings-plan tiers. The report's 2-vCPU/4-GB and $0.000114/second inputs are explicitly estimate_unverified_rates; client wall time is not billable resource time and billing_verified=false. Do not use them as a bill or observed hardware inventory. Runtime-only idle-time wording must not be assumed to apply to sandbox idle time; lifecycle docs say sandboxes are billed while they exist. No historical price increase is asserted without comparable dated evidence. GKE/Compute Engine alternatives have their own pricing, not these rates.
